item.title: Arboretum Foundation and UW Botanic Gardens unite after decades of partnership
item.description: The Arboretum Foundation and the University of Washington Botanic Gardens will combine operations under a single nonprofit organization: Seattle Botanic Gardens.

item.title: UW recognized across all campuses with Carnegie Foundation Community Engagement reclassification
item.description: The University of Washington has again earned a prestigious recognition for the impact and importance of the connections faculty, students and staff have with local, regional and global communities.

item.title: ArtSci Roundup: February
item.description: Come curious. Leave inspired. While February might be just 28 days, the UW offers an exciting lineup of more than 40 in-person and online events. item.title: Q&A: Wildfire in protected NW Forests highlights need for strategy updates
item.description: University of Washington researchers show that wildfire is increasingly impacting lands managed under the Northwest Forest Plan, a seminal measure enacted in 1994 to preserve habitat for endangered species.

item.title: Q&A: A UW materials lab probes the mysteries of toughness at the nano scale
item.description: Lucas Meza, an assistant professor of mechanical engineering at the University of Washington, started his lab to build a new generation of tough and light nanomaterials inspired by natural materials like wood, shell and bone. Instead, he discovered “big gaps” in our basic understanding of what makes a material tough or brittle. Meza spoke to UW News about his strange and surprising journey into the nano realm.

item.title: UW astronomers spot record-breaking asteroid in Rubin Observatory data
item.description: A team led by University of Washington astronomers has discovered the fastest-ever spinning asteroid with a diameter over half a kilometer.

item.title: Q&A: UW researchers create a smart glove with its own sense of touch
item.description: A new smart glove from the UW Wearable Intelligence Lab could help physical therapy patients track progress and train robotic hands to grasp.

item.title: Astronomers discover ancient barred spiral galaxy
item.description: New research supported by Yingjie Cheng, a University of Washington postdoctoral researcher in astronomy, uncovered a contender for one of the earliest observed spiral galaxies containing a stellar bar — a notable visual feature that can play an important role in the evolution of a galaxy.

item.title: In a study, AI model OpenScholar synthesizes scientific research and cites sources as accurately as human experts
item.description: A UW and Ai2 research team built OpenScholar, an open-source AI model designed specifically to synthesize current scientific research. In tests, OpenScholar cited sources as accurately as human experts, and 16 scientists preferred its response to those written by subject experts 51% of the time.
